venue.name: Freshwater Fisheries Society of B.C.
venue.description: The Freshwater Fisheries Society of BC was registered under the B.C. Societies Act in March 2003, taking over fish culture, fish health and other biological and technical services from the province's hatchery program. It owns and operates six major fish hatcheries, located in Duncan, Abbotsford, Summerland, Clearwater, Fort Steele and Vanderhoof, and says most of its hatcheries welcome visitors and offer self-guided tours. Its Corporate Services division, and the address in the tracker, is the Victoria corporate office at 80 Regatta Landing; the Society's own school field trips, group Learn to Fish sessions and fishing birthday parties are delivered at the Abbotsford, Summerland, Clearwater and Fort Steele hatcheries and at select off-site lake locations, not in Victoria. The Society also lends fishing rods and tackle free of charge from a list of locations that includes the Victoria corporate office and the Vancouver Island Trout Hatchery in Duncan.
venue.address: 80 Regatta Landing, Suite 101, Victoria, B.C. V9A 7S2

facility_notes.lunch_space: Students are invited to bring a snack or lunch. Please dress for the weather, as outdoor programs run rain or shine.

venue.seasonal_notes: School field trips and group Learn to Fish sessions are available year-round (limited availability November - February) at the Abbotsford hatchery, and seasonally (May - August) at the Summerland, Clearwater and Fort Steele hatcheries and select off-site locations.

programs.name: It's a Trout's Life (school field trip)
programs.description: Kids join Myki the rainbow trout to discover the adventures fish face on their journey from egg to adult. The site describes the program as hands-on, including an interactive story board, role playing, drawing, a tour of the hatchery and a nature walk to the on-site ponds. Published duration is 1 - 2 hours. Available year-round (limited availability November - February) at the Abbotsford hatchery and from May - August at the Summerland and Fort Steele hatcheries; none of these is on Vancouver Island. The School Field Trips page says "For most programs we can accommodate up to two classes at the same time" without giving a headcount, and that all prices include GST/PST. Booking is by the contact form with 'Field Trip' selected as the topic; the site notes that submitting the form is not a confirmation of booking.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a rainbow trout's life story on an interactive story board, take a role in the story and draw, then walk through the hatchery and out to the ponds on site.
programs.our_note: This one is not a Victoria outing: the Society's Victoria address is an office, and It's a Trout's Life runs at Abbotsford, Summerland and Fort Steele. The Vancouver Island hatchery in Duncan is not listed as a location for it, so ask whether anything equivalent runs there before you plan around it.
programs.practical_summary: The $5 per child price includes GST/PST and children bring their own snack or lunch; outdoor parts run rain or shine. Washrooms, indoor backup, capacity numbers and how much notice is needed are not stated, and the program locations are all off Vancouver Island.

programs.name: Learn to Fish (school field trip)
programs.description: Participants learn about freshwater habitats, conservation and how to fish responsibly, with lessons on fish identification and biology, fishing techniques and equipment set-up, safety, proper fish handling, and a hatchery tour, ending with catch and release trout fishing at the on-site ponds or a local lake. Published duration is 3 - 4 hours. Price is given only as "Location dependent", so no figure is recorded here. Available year-round (limited availability November - February) at the Abbotsford hatchery, and for May - August dates at the Clearwater and Fort Steele hatcheries as well as select off-site locations across B.C. Booking is by the contact form with 'Field Trip' selected as the topic.
programs.what_children_do: Learn to identify fish and set up tackle, handle rods and gear, walk through the hatchery, then fish catch-and-release at the on-site ponds or a local lake.
programs.our_note: Three to four hours outdoors with rods is a long stretch for the youngest end of the Kindergarten-to-12 range, and the price is quoted per location rather than published, so get it in writing early. Nothing on this page is offered on Vancouver Island.
programs.practical_summary: No price is published for this one - it is quoted by location - and no capacity, notice period or washroom information is given. Children bring their own snack or lunch, and the outdoor parts run rain or shine.
programs.extra_fees_note: Price is published only as "Location dependent". The page adds "*All prices include GST/PST".

programs.name: Group Learn to Fish booking
programs.description: Learn to Fish programs for organized groups of all ages and abilities, covering the basics of freshwater fishing including angling ethics, tackle selection, and fishing and casting techniques. All equipment is provided and every session includes hands-on fishing time. Available year-round (limited availability November - February) at the Abbotsford hatchery and seasonally (May - August) at the Clearwater and Fort Steele hatcheries, as well as select off-site lake locations across B.C. Price is published only as "Location-dependent". Booking is by the contact form with 'Group Learn to Fish bookings' selected as the topic; the site notes that submitting the form is not a confirmation of booking.
programs.what_children_do: Choose tackle and set up a rod, practise casting, and fish with equipment the Society provides at a hatchery pond or a lake.
programs.our_note: This is the route for a daycare or club rather than a school class, and the group version publishes no price at all - ask for a written quote for your headcount and location. Bring your own washroom plan if the session is at an off-site lake.
programs.practical_summary: Equipment is provided and every session includes fishing time, but no price, group size, age minimum or notice period is published, and the locations are all off Vancouver Island.
programs.evidence: Learn to Fish programs for organized groups of all ages and abilities.

programs.name: Fishing birthday party
programs.description: A 2.5 hour party that includes a tour of the hatchery (subject to availability), hands-on fishing instruction at the stocked ponds, all the tackle and equipment needed, and a fishing rod gift for the birthday child. Food, cake and candles are not provided but may be brought; a barbeque is available on request at select locations. The price is $200 for up to 15 children, with $10 per child for additional children. Available at the fishing ponds at the Abbotsford, Clearwater and Fort Steele hatcheries - year-round at Abbotsford and seasonally (May - August) at Clearwater and Fort Steele. Booking is by the contact form with 'Birthday Party' selected as the topic.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the hatchery, then fish at the stocked pond with rods and tackle the staff hand out and set up.
programs.our_note: The $200 covers up to fifteen children as a flat fee, so a small group pays the same as a big one; each extra child is $10. Cake and food are your job, and the barbeque is only at some sites - ask when you enquire.
programs.practical_summary: Two and a half hours with equipment provided and a flat $200 group price for up to 15 children. Washrooms, indoor shelter and how far ahead to book are not stated, and all three locations are off Vancouver Island.
programs.extra_fees_note: $200 for up to 15 children. $10/ child for additional children.
programs.evidence: PRICE: $200 for up to 15 children. $10/ child for additional children.

programs.name: Rod Loan
programs.description: A free equipment loan rather than a visit: families and other groups can borrow spinning rods with reels and a basic box of tackle at no cost. Rod Loan locations are Society hatcheries plus a number of tourism visitor centres and tackle shops throughout the province. The listed locations include the Freshwater Fisheries Society of BC Corporate Office at 80 Regatta Landing, Suite 101, Victoria, and the Vancouver Island Trout Hatchery at 1080 Wharncliffe Road, Duncan; both are marked "Contact us in advance to coordinate". The program is supported by Luhr Jensen. Nothing is published about how many rods a group may borrow, for how long, or whether a deposit is needed.
programs.our_note: This is the only entry on the Society's site that a Victoria group can actually use locally - you collect gear from the Regatta Landing office rather than attend a program, and the site says to contact them in advance to coordinate. A B.C. fishing licence still applies to the adults; check who in your group needs one before you go.
programs.practical_summary: Rods and a basic tackle box are lent free from the Victoria corporate office and the Duncan hatchery, by prior arrangement. Numbers of rods, loan length, deposits and any age limits are not published.
programs.evidence: At no cost, you can borrow spinning rods with reels and a basic box of tackle.

gaps: This record is the Society itself. Its Victoria address is the corporate office at 80 Regatta Landing; no program on the site is delivered there apart from Rod Loan pickup. School field trips, group Learn to Fish and birthday parties run at the Abbotsford, Summerland, Clearwater and Fort Steele hatcheries and at select off-site lakes - none on Vancouver Island. The Vancouver Island Trout Hatchery in Duncan is a separate tracker row.

No booking email or booking phone is published for programs; every program page routes to the same web form. The Contact page does list a corporate office line, 250-414-4200 (toll free 888-601-4200), and separate hatchery numbers, but the site does not present these as a booking route.
Price for the Learn to Fish school field trip and for group bookings is published only as "Location dependent" / "Location-dependent", so no figure could be recorded.
Capacity is not given as a number. The School Field Trips page says only "For most programs we can accommodate up to two classes at the same time".
Minimum booking notice (lead time) is not stated for any program.

No washroom, indoor lunch space or rain-backup information is published for any program location. The School Field Trips page says only that students may bring a snack or lunch and that outdoor programs run rain or shine.
Youngest age welcomed is not stated in years anywhere; It's a Trout's Life is published by grade as "Preschool, Kindergarten to 2".
No chaperone ratio, deposit, payment timing or cancellation policy is published.
Duration is published as a range ("1 - 2 hours", "3 - 4 hours"); duration_min records the lower bound and the range is repeated in each description.
Accessibility, stroller access and bus parking are not addressed anywhere on the site.
